notes.LsaDisablePasswordLessCurrentUser: console XDefiant 0x2f70: NdrClientCall3(lsarpc proxy 0x3d978, opnum 0x7f, generic binding with NULL server -> RpcBindingCreateW ncalrpc LSARPC_ENDPOINT, authn level 6 WINNT from template 0x41b00); RPC exception -> I_RpcMapWin32Status(code) when negative, else 0xC0000001. Server (Fortnite lsasrv 0xbff80 -> 0xbfd8c) behind security callback 0x24dd0 with .data 0x15e4f0 entry {mask 8, flags 3}: opnum >= 0x81 or flag 4 -> 0x6d1, protseq bit clear -> 0x6a7, IsClientLocal != 1 or authn level 2-4 -> 5, flag 2: authn service 0x44 at level >= 5 passes, else CheckTokenMembershipEx(CTMF_INCLUDE_LPAC) on well-known slot 22 = S-1-5-11 (builder 0x4f820 entry 24: authority 0x15ed74 = 5, RID 11; FALSE -> GetLastError, not a member -> 5), then TokenIsAppContainer without flag 8 -> 5; the client gets the code as an RPC exception and returns I_RpcMapWin32Status of it (5 -> 0xC0000022). Console title token: gamehostservice 0x2c40 NtCreateUserProcess passes only JobList/ClientId/ImageName/MemoryReserve attributes (no token, no lowbox), so the title inherits the service primary token; 0x4c5c only adds the XBOX://LI security attribute -> not an AppContainer, member of Authenticated Users, gate passes (token user S-1-5-18 and the other groups are inferred, only S-1-5-11 membership and the AppContainer flag are proven). Body: ForceDisablePasswordlessNewDevices (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Cryptography\PwdlessPlat\ImageCustomization, absent from every shipped console hive) unset -> HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\PasswordLess\Device DevicePasswordLessBuildVersion = 0 (0x108924/0x108530); set -> ...\PasswordLess\UserConfig\<token user> PasswordLess = 2 (0x1086fc); write error -> 0xC007xxxx, else STATUS_SUCCESS. Written to the emulated HKLM store (TOMBOX_GDK_ROOT or %LOCALAPPDATA%\XboxEmulator, hklm\<key>\<value>.dword), read back by the console-mode title registry hook in compat-common; host LSA and registry never touched

Written to the emulated HKLM store (TOMBOX_GDK_ROOT or %LOCALAPPDATA%\XboxEmulator, hklm\<key>\<value>.dword), read back by the console-mode title registry hook in compat-common; host LSA and registry never touched

notes.XDspActivate: type 1 convolution (XDefiant) runs on the host with the console validation; types 2 (FFT) and 3 (IFFT) pass the console descriptor checks and then return E_NOTIMPL: their DSP microcode and buffer layout are not in any dump (see docs/BLOCKERS.md, chad FFT/IFFT streams)
notes.XDspConnectWithMaximumStreamLimit: console 0x2bc0: E_INVALIDARG for mem/size/activations, streams > 0x100 or priority > 2, then E_POINTER for a null out; XDspConnect is this call with 0x100 streams, priority 2 (console 0x2b90); limits kept per client, the CPU convolution has no hardware stream queue to apply them to
notes.XDspSubmitCommandWithEnvelope: console 0x3200 -> 0x2524 (shared with XDspSubmitCommand 0x31e0, envelope NULL): for convolution streams the envelope is taken at the first command of every 8 (counter +0x150 & 7) and must lie in the XDspConnect memory (APU translation 0x1888 fails -> E_INVALIDARG); later commands in the group reuse a snapshot and a NULL envelope at a group start disables it. The DSP microcode that applies it is not in any dump, so the gain math is inferred from the GDK description (per-block gains applied during convolution, left then right): IR partition k is scaled by gain[k], right gains at roundup4(partitions). Known gaps vs console: the console snapshot holds only 0x20 bytes per channel and takes the right half at envelope+[+0x148]*4, and +0x148 is not confirmed to equal the partition count

notes.FwpmBitmapIndexFree0: client port of console FWPUCLNT 0x9bf0: NULL engine returns FWP_E_NULL_POINTER 0x8032001C (direct, no RPC); a title process has no bfe.dll loaded, so the console takes the NdrClientCall3 opnum 0xc2 path (FwpmEngineOpen0 sets engine+0x70 to the direct dispatch only when GetModuleHandleExW(bfe.dll) succeeds), whose format string (no comm/fault status, ref GUID + in ref UINT8) makes a NULL mapId/index raise RPC_X_NULL_REF_POINTER 1780 in the caller; service = console BFE.DLL 0x3e950 reached via BfeGetDirectDispatchTable+0x70 -> 0x3bd4c: *index >= 0x40 or a map GUID other than FWPM_CONDITION_IP_LOCAL_ADDRESS / IP_LOCAL_PORT / IP_REMOTE_ADDRESS / IP_REMOTE_PORT gives STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER, which the RPC server stub raises (0x47e8 RpcRaiseException for user-mode callers) and the client re-raises noncontinuable 0xC000000D (no SEH in the console client); otherwise btr of the bit in that map's 64-bit bitmap under the service lock, no double-free check, returns 0; the four bitmaps are BFE-global (one per service, zeroed at BFE start), emulated process-global; engine identity is not checked beyond NULL because the emulator has no emulated FwpmEngineOpen0 (titles get PC FWPUCLNT engines) and the console checks it only as an RPC context handle inside the host-side BFE, which this crate must not contact; the BFE session-entry lock (0xc800, transaction wait) is not modelled since emulated callers have no BFE transactions
notes.FwpmBitmapIndexGet0: client port of console FWPUCLNT 0x9cb0: NULL engine returns FWP_E_NULL_POINTER 0x8032001C; RPC path NdrClientCall3 opnum 0xc1 (ref GUID in, simple-ref UINT8 out), NULL mapId/index raise RPC_X_NULL_REF_POINTER 1780; service = console BFE.DLL 0x3eba0 via BfeGetDirectDispatchTable+0x68 -> 0x3bdf0: for the four maps (IP_LOCAL_ADDRESS, IP_LOCAL_PORT, IP_REMOTE_ADDRESS, IP_REMOTE_PORT, GUIDs read from BFE .rdata 0xa2ce0/0xa2f00/0xa2cf0/0xa2f10) sets and returns the lowest clear bit of that map's 64-bit bitmap, a full bitmap or any other GUID writes 0xFF and still returns 0 (the service always returns STATUS_SUCCESS); BFE-global state emulated process-global; engine handle and session-lock limits as for FwpmBitmapIndexFree0

notes.DebugLive: console hix_xs.dll from the newest title dump (TOMBOX_HIX_XS_CONSOLE, hix_xs_console.dll beside this DLL) bound to the in-process XgsKmd10 emulation as for InitializeHix; (DWORD, const summary*, out*) -> HRESULT (Trackmania 0x55e0, XDefiant 0x7210, absent from the 19041 Fortnite build): logs "Checking the possibility of live debugging" and runs 0x4ec34, which posts mailbox cmd 0x1b; the emulated KMD serves only cmds 0xf (summary), 0x17 (disarm), 0x28/0x29 (halt/unhalt all shader waves) and answers every other command, 0x1b included, with status E_NOTIMPL (0x80004001) and no stream, because it holds no Xbox wave state, so the console code takes its no-live-debugging path and returns E_FAIL; E_FAIL without a console image; test tests_dump::console_debug_live_reports_no_live_debugging

notes.WriteHangDump: console hix_xs.dll from the newest title dump (TOMBOX_HIX_XS_CONSOLE, hix_xs_console.dll beside this DLL) bound to the in-process XgsKmd10 emulation as for InitializeHix, d:/t: mapped under TOMBOX_SCRATCH_DIR or %LOCALAPPDATA%\TomBox\scratch\<title>; (DWORD flags, PWSTR out, DWORD cch, const summary*) -> HRESULT (Trackmania 0x5930, XDefiant 0x7560, Fortnite 19041 ordinal 4 0x5060): creates <d:|t:>\HIX\gpuhang-Y-M-D-h-m-s.hix (flags bit 2 picks d:) with magic "Hix" version 0x220200 and the TicI block, then the capture 0x7439c: halt all waves (cmd 0x28, served), SQ dump (cmd 0x14), which the emulated KMD answers with E_NOTIMPL because it holds no Xbox wave, IH-ring or VM state, so the capture stops, waves are unhalted (cmd 0x29) and the SysI block is written; on that failed capture the console code (0x5d0a) skips the d:\gpuhang-latest.hix copy, the high-level summary and the path copy-out and still returns S_OK, so the .hix holds only the header, TicI, Basc and SysI blocks with no GPU state and the out buffer is left untouched; E_FAIL only when CreateFileW fails or without a console image; a full dump needs the emulator to model wave, IH-ring and VM state (docs/BLOCKERS.md); test tests_dump::console_write_hang_dump_takes_its_failed_capture_path

Core: *Registration = 0 first, then under the module critical section (0xa900) a first-use init that subscribes the four PLM WNF state names (0x4a1c: RtlQueryWnfStateData then RtlSubscribeWnfStateChangeNotification, error -> RtlNtStatusToDosError returned); allocates a 0x48-byte entry (refcount 1 at +0x38, routine +0x20, context +0x28, id +0x30) or returns 8 (ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY); the id is one process-wide counter (0xa8a0) shared by both registration kinds, starting at 1; entry appended to the list tail; *Registration = id; returns 0. Here: compat-common os_host::plm::register(Constrained) in the os_host owner module (all compat DLLs must be built from the same compat-common so the owner publishes the register entry) (cross-module through TOMBOX_OSHOST_PLM_REGISTER), the same id counter, list and refcount/active-thread scheme. The emulator PLM signals (window minimise/restore watcher, TOMBOX_PLM_DIR command file, plm::set_constrained) stand in for the WNF names 0x41c60d2aa3bc2875 (constrained TRUE) and 0x41c60d2aa3bc3075 (constrained FALSE). Known deviation: the console writes *Registration without a NULL check (a NULL pointer faults); here NULL returns 87 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and registers nothing
notes.RegisterAppStateChangeNotification: console thunk RVA 0x4f40 (Fortnite image; XDefiant thunk 0x5a90) -> the same register core 0x4b80 with the app-state list (.data 0xa988). Signature ULONG (PAPPSTATE_CHANGE_ROUTINE Routine, PVOID Context, PAPPSTATE_REGISTRATION* Registration); routine is VOID (BOOLEAN Quiesced, PVOID Context). Same core as ordinal 1: shared id counter, entry appended, *Registration = id, returns 0. Delivery (WNF callback 0x48f0 -> dispatch 0x4790): WNF 0x41c60d2aa3bc1875 -> Quiesced = TRUE (suspend), 0x41c60d2aa3bc2075 -> Quiesced = FALSE (resume); every registration of that kind is snapshotted under the lock, addref'd and marked with the delivering thread id (+0x3c); one registration is called directly on the notification thread (0x45cc), several are fanned out to threadpool work items in a cleanup group and waited for (0x4650), falling back to sequential calls if the threadpool fails. Here: os_host::plm::register(AppState) in the owner; plm::suspend/resume (and the suspend timeout watch in os_host::quiesce) deliver on a separate notification thread, one registration inline and several in parallel threads joined before the signal returns. Same NULL-Registration deviation as ordinal 1
notes.UnregisterAppConstrainedChangeNotificati: console thunk RVA 0x4fa0 (Fortnite image; XDefiant thunk 0x5af0) -> unregister core 0x4dd8 with the constrained list. VOID (PAPPCONSTRAIN_REGISTRATION Registration) on the console; the exported function returns a ULONG here (0, or 0x490 ERROR_NOT_FOUND) which a VOID caller ignores. Core: if never initialised returns at once; else under the lock finds the entry whose id (+0x30) matches in this kind's list (an id of the other kind is not found: wil log, 0x490), unlinks it, leaves the lock, then WaitOnAddress until the entry's active-thread field (+0x3c) is 0 or the calling thread (so an in-flight callback finishes first, and unregistering from inside the callback does not deadlock), drops the reference, and when both lists are empty unsubscribes the WNF names (RtlUnsubscribeWnfNotificationWaitForCompletion) and clears the init flag. Here: os_host::plm::unregister(Constrained) in the owner, same find/unlink/wait-for-in-flight behaviour; after it returns no further callback is made for that registration

notes.CloseTrace: PC CloseTrace (via System32 advapi32) wrapped with the console sechost 0xba40/0xb9ac consumer-table rules: handle 0 or INVALID_PROCESSTRACE_HANDLE returns ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE 6; a table entry in ProcessTrace (state 1) becomes state 2, the PC consumer is closed and ERROR_CTX_CLOSE_PENDING 7007 is returned; state 2 returns 6; an idle entry is unlinked and the PC CloseTrace result returned; handles not in the table go straight to the PC
notes.EtwQueryRealtimeConsumer: port of console sechost 0x4ad40: handle 0 or INVALID_PROCESSTRACE_HANDLE (handle-1 above -3 unsigned) returns ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE 6 before any pointer check; NULL EventsLost or BuffersLost out returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER 87; under the consumer-table lock (0x4a878/0xb97c list walk on the handle at ctx+0x10) a missing entry or an entry whose ProcessTraceMode (ctx+0x6c, copied from EVENT_TRACE_LOGFILEW+0x1c at OpenTraceW) lacks PROCESS_TRACE_MODE_REAL_TIME 0x100 returns 6, else writes ctx+0x288 and ctx+0x28c and returns 0; those two counters are the ETW_REALTIME_CONSUMER EventsLostCount/BuffersLostCount pointers the console hands to NtTraceControl in ProcessTrace's realtime connect (0xa090; member order per Geoff Chappell's ETW_REALTIME_CONSUMER notes), zero from OpenTraceW until then; the emulated table is filled by the OpenTraceW hook here, but realtime delivery stays in the PC ProcessTrace, whose kernel connection updates the PC sechost's own counters, so the emulated counters stay at their OpenTraceW value of 0 even when the host kernel drops events
notes.OpenTraceW: PC OpenTraceW (via System32 advapi32) opens the consumer so PC ProcessTrace can deliver events; each successful open is registered in the emulated console consumer table (console sechost 0xb1c8: list append under the table lock, state 0, counters 0) under the returned handle with the caller's ProcessTraceMode read before the call, the way console OpenTraceW is the only creator of table entries
notes.ProcessTrace: PC ProcessTrace wrapped with console sechost 0xb6e0 table rules: every table entry named must be idle, otherwise ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE 6 with no processing and the entries marked so far restored; entries go to state 1 for the call and back to 0 afterwards, and entries a CloseTrace moved to state 2 are freed when it returns; handles not in the table are passed through unmarked

notes.WldpCheckSecurityWatermarkState: Fortnite console RVA 0x14ab0, walked end to end on 2026-11-21. Deterministic parts: the DMCfgUtils.dll hash path 0x1443c returns 1 with all-zero 0x20-byte hashes, and FVEAPI (0x14130, delay-load 0x28068/0x28070) cannot load. Neither DLL is in any shipped console image (Fortnite, XDefiant, Trackmania, Terraria). The watermark files are %SystemDrive%\DPP\WatermarkHSTITestComplete.bin and WatermarkSBTestComplete.bin (0x14594 read, 0x14930 write, 0x14364 delete). The Non-Production Errors.txt writer is 0x1479c/0x146b8 (0x252-byte header 0x1f170). The result is *out = 0 only when ManufacturingMode is off, no banned BCD element was found, Secure Boot passed (edi) and HSTI verified (r15b). Otherwise *out = 1, and on 0 Non-Production Errors.txt is deleted. That decision needs runtime answers that no image file holds, and none can be sourced for a title process: (1) ZwFilterBootOption(1, 0x10200003, elements 0x260000a0/0x16000010/0x16000049/0x260000f2) and (1, 0x10200002, 0x16000010/0x16000049), where a hit is status 0, 0x10000000 or 0x80430006; (2) GetOsManufacturingMode; (3) HSTI: the KdDebuggerEnabled override value (0x16abc RegGetValueW) and the NtQuerySystemInformation 0xA6 result blob parsed by 0x15bd0; (4) Secure Boot 0x12714: NtQuerySystemInformation 0x91 and 0x8F, NtQuerySystemEnvironmentValueEx UEFI variables behind AdjustTokenPrivileges (0x12594/0x12260), the three 0x123c0 checks over .data 0x25020, and the registry reads 0x157d8/0x1586c. Choosing values that make the checks pass would fake the retail result, so the export stays missing until the emulated console state for (1)-(4) has a source
notes.WldpSendSmartAppControlBlockToast: Trackmania console RVA 0x1c010: the wil feature-staging check (feature 0x259f533, .data 0x41230, 0x1c0bc) picks toasthelper.cpp builder 0x1b80c or 0x1b9f4. Both builders start the same way. They take a WindowsCreateStringReference of Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.XmlDocument (0x32610) and call RoActivateInstance (0x19d68). On failure they report it through wil (0x2246c, lines 0x195 and 0x1c5) and return that HRESULT, before any template, mui string or ToastNotifier is touched. On the console that activation fails. Every shipped console SOFTWARE hive has WindowsRuntime\ActivatableClassId but no Windows.Data.Xml.Dom class, and System32 has no msxml6.dll. So combase's lookup gives REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG 0x80040154. A thread with no apartment, and no implicit MTA in the process, gets CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED 0x800401F0 first; that state is probed with CoGetApartmentType, which matched RoActivateInstance in every state on the PC. The emulator returns exactly that and never activates the PC XmlDocument or notifier, so no host toast appears.

notes.WldpIsProductionConfigurationInProc: Trackmania console RVA 0x14f10. The first helper, 0x7c08, writes a flag word and an HRESULT. If the flags are 0, the export takes the fast path 0x15299: *out = ((flags & mask) == 0), so production = 1. It then writes the State-provider event (metadata 0x35e9b, provider .data 0x40270, keyword 0x800000000000) and returns 0x7c08's HRESULT. 0x7c08 is not a static table decode. It is an 11,592-line obfuscated routine (0x1290-byte frame, lock cmpxchg on .data 0x411a8, about 70 CFG-dispatched indirect calls through 0x2f230). Its output depends on runtime queries: NtQuerySystemInformation resolved with GetProcAddress at 0xab46 and 0x127ec, GetProcessMitigationPolicy(GetCurrentProcess, 0xb) at 0x84cf, GetModuleFileNameW of the wldp image at 0xc66a, and GetModuleHandleExW/FreeLibrary module probes. Its output cannot be computed offline, so the 0x343a2 data cannot be committed as a decoded table. Porting it means porting the whole routine and modelling those queries as the console answers them for a title, which is unknown (the same class of state as row 8). The slow path, which reads CodeIntegrity\Data Watermark*.bin, hashes HSTI and Security (0x13f70/0x14210), rewrites them (0x147c8) and shows the WinSta0\Default warning, is gated on the same flags
